title: ia position prints the position body for a scope key; the key's word no longer filters the reserved rules
summary:
@inventarch/cli adds the consumer verb ia position [--seat ] [--shape ] [--phase

] [--depth ] [--budget ] [--word ] [--json], which prints the runtime's position for the scope key its flags name, read through the whole-workspace scope: no flag is K0, the repository's `@workspace` at shape context, phase orient, depth 0 and budget 0, and a key naming any part takes normalizeScopeKey's defaults for the rest. A --seat that spells a canonical identity is that record; any other is a location, workspace-relative or absolute inside the root, and ./ makes a path spelled as an identity a location. Human output prints the seat and the body's revision, the key used, the capture's freshness (current, stale or no-capture), the body's digest and counts, then the loaded records, the pointers and their tallies, the rules and playbooks that apply by word with their tallies, the playbook cells, the rules reserved outside the budget, the mandates, the frontier and the unknowns, and last the two widening keys as ia position commands with --root as given: one hop deeper (absent at depth 2) and the re-seat template --seat at depth 1 and budget 16. With --json it prints one line {version: 1, ok: true, body, digest, hostNote}, the Door's position result byte for byte. It opens the workspace without the db cache, needs no capture and writes nothing. Its refusals keep the runtime's code, IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID, and message, and each names one command, with --root as given where that command takes one: a shape or phase outside its closed set, or a depth or budget outside its cap, is refused at exit 2 before the workspace is read, naming the same call with the closed set or the cap in that part's place; a word the closure does not register (exit 1) names ia vocabulary, which takes no --root; and a seat the workspace does not admit or a path outside it (exit 1) names ia position. ia position is a consumer verb, not a machine route: LEGACY_OPERATIONS, the usage line, ia --help and --schema and ia scope in every form are unchanged. ia next now names ia position --seat for a seat that is no plan, milestone or task, and ia position --seat --shape sequence for a require cycle, at the record the runtime names, where it named ia inspect and ia next. ia read reads the path of an absolute : locator by the rule --seat reads a path with: an in-root name that only begins with .., such as ..cache, reads as the relative path it names, and the root itself as ., so such a locator is refused as its relative spelling is rather than as a path outside the root; a locator that resolved before reads as before. @inventarch/runtime: positionBody no longer filters by the key's word the blocking rules reserved in rules, the appliesByWord section with its tallies, the cells or the mandates. rules is taken from the candidates without the word, so a blocking rule that claims a location or applies by its subject-word is reserved under any word, and appliesByWord lists rules and playbooks of every word that apply to what loads under the word or to a reserved rule; the word still restricts loaded, pointers, pointerTallies and frontier. The word parameter of the position row in MACHINE_PROTOCOL version 2, which the MCP ia_position tool carries as its inputSchema description, says the same. The seat refusals positionBody throws now carry next, ia position, or ia inspect for a seat at runtime placement that is the repository's own `@workspace`, which the Door named before; the Door's answers are unchanged. The package root and @inventarch/runtime/internal/scope-key export rootRelative(root, path), the absolute-path rule a location seat and ia read share. readBody refuses a line locator at the workspace root itself, such as .:3, as a directory and no source, where its message ended with an empty path. Limits: no seat at runtime placement reaches ia position, since the workspace session the CLI opens places no source at runtime, and the host note reports no installed state and no CLI id@version.
